hero.lead: Soil water stress is a silent crisis: it cuts harvests, dries up watering holes and drains aquifers. NASA satellites measure it every month. We turn those measurements into statistical evidence anyone can read.
hero.statsLabel: Key facts about the published data
hero.source: Source: NASA GES DISC, via Giovanni

problem.title: What happens when the soil dries out?
problem.lead: Soil moisture is the water reserve that crops, pastures and, deeper down, aquifers depend on. When it declines over time, the effects cascade.

cards.title: Agriculture
cards.text: Soil that loses moisture cuts yields from the moment seeds sprout. Farmers compensate with irrigation that draws even harder on already fragile resources.

cards.title: Ecosystems and livestock
cards.text: Drought empties ponds and reservoirs. Livestock walk further to drink, and wetland habitats shrink.

cards.title: Underground wealth
cards.text: Less water seeps in, and aquifers recharge poorly. This depletion is invisible: you cannot see water you never see disappear.

mission.titleStart: NASA provides the data. We provide the
mission.lead: Every conclusion on the platform can be traced back to the satellite measurement behind it.

cards.title: Satellite data
cards.text: Soil moisture, soil temperature and evaporation are modelled by GLDAS from space observations, then averaged over the city by Giovanni.

cards.title: Statistical proof
cards.text: The Mann-Kendall test tells whether a trend is real or due to chance; the Theil-Sen slope tells how fast it moves.

cards.title: Explainable AI
cards.text: The assistant answers from the platform's own calculations and cites its sources. It never makes up a number.

about.title: About Terra Sense Cameroun
intro: Terra Sense Cameroun is an observatory of soil water stress, built for challenge 02 of the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It makes satellite series readable that are usually explored in specialist tools.

The visualisation colours the territory of Yaoundé, bounded by its seven districts, according to the value measured in the chosen month. Colours glide from one month to the next, but no value is invented between two dates.
For each variable, the platform tests for a trend and estimates its speed. Non-significant results are shown as such.
The conversational assistant relies on the same calculations. When it does not know, it says so.

methods.name: Mann-Kendall
methods.text: Compares each measurement with every later one to tell whether the series rises or falls consistently. The Hamed and Rao correction accounts for the autocorrelation of successive months. Threshold: p < 0.05.

methods.name: Theil-Sen
methods.text: Median of the slopes between all pairs of measurements. It gives the speed of change, per year or per decade, and resists extreme values.

methods.name: SHAP
methods.text: Assigns each factor (rain, evaporation, temperature) its share of a prediction. This reading is shown only when a model is published for the area.
